sections.html:
Pocatello is the home of Idaho State University, in the Portneuf Valley of southeastern Idaho. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 58,771 residents, only 3.6 percent above April 2020, so the market moves at a calmer pace than the Treasure Valley or North Idaho.

Prices are modest. Survey data for 2020 to 2024 shows a $271,000 median value for owner-occupied units, 64.5 percent owner occupancy and $948 median gross rent. One house can land far from a citywide median in either direction.

Pocatello grew around the Union Pacific Railroad and sits along the Portneuf River. A house beside the old rail corridor invites questions about noise and condition, and one near the river invites questions about drainage. Prepare answers if either fits yours.

Pocatello's nickname, the Gate City, came from pioneers passing through the Portneuf Gap, and the railroad later made the city a transportation junction. The Portneuf Greenway trail runs more than 15 miles along the river, which buyers who like walking and cycling notice, so mention it if your house is nearby.

Pocatello took in the neighboring city of Alameda in 1962. Chubbuck, to the north, turned down a similar merger and is still a separate city, so a Chubbuck address follows that city's rules and not Pocatello's.

Part of Pocatello reaches into Power County, where the school district is American Falls Joint School District 381 and not the Pocatello Chubbuck district. Find out which jurisdiction holds your parcel before you request permit or tax records.

Summers run hot and winters bite, from a record high of 104 degrees to a record low of minus 33 on February 1, 1985. Foundation design here assumes a 3 foot frost level, which hints at how deep the ground freezes. Frost heave can crack slabs, shift garage floors and open gaps at foundation edges.

  • Walk the foundation and look for diagonal cracks or doors that stick.
  • Check the garage slab and exterior concrete for lifting.
  • Check the roof after a heavy snow year and write down when it was last repaired.

Foundation and roof are the first things buyers raise. A cash buyer accounts for them in the offer instead of making you fix them.

The Bannock County part of Pocatello is in the Pocatello Chubbuck School District 25, with three public high schools, four middle schools and thirteen elementary schools. Families can also choose from two public charters and several private schools.

Commercial flights use Pocatello Regional Airport. City buses from Pocatello Regional Transit cover five hourly routes, Monday to Saturday only, with nothing in the evening or on Sunday.

New construction, remodels and dangerous building abatement all go through the city Building Department. Submit applications in the eTRAKiT online portal or call 208-234-6158. Local amendments sit on top of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, and the fee schedule is republished every fiscal year.

  • Find out whether earlier work on the house was permitted. Inspectors raise it.
  • A dangerous building notice on the property should be disclosed at once, since it restricts a buyer's plans.
  • Save contractor receipts for the roof, furnace and water heater. They date the major systems.

Tax bills leave the treasurer's office by the fourth Monday in November. December 20 is the deadline for a full-year or first-half payment, and June 20 of the next year is the second half. When either falls on a weekend, payment is due the next business day.

Bannock County dateWhat happens
April 15Property Tax Reduction program applications close
First Monday in JuneNotices of assessment go out
June 20Second half of the prior year is due
Fourth Monday in JuneAppeals to the Board of Equalization must be filed
Second Monday in JulyBoard hearings end
Fourth Monday in NovemberTreasurer mails bills
December 20Full payment or first half is due
December 31Current year homeowner's exemption applications close

A late second half costs 1 percent per month, counted from January 1. Pay even a few days late and you may owe about six months of interest. New construction and occupancy are billed on their own roll, mailed in January and due in February.

At appeal, the Board of Equalization tests whether market value is fair and accurate. Hardship does not lower a value. Visit the treasurer in Room 203 of the Bannock County Courthouse, 624 E. Center St., or call 208-236-7260. The county's Property Tax Hub walks through each step.

Unpaid tax does not block a sale. The title company reads the county record, finds anything delinquent and pays it from your proceeds at closing. The cost of waiting is the interest, which keeps building from January 1 on a late second half.

If you are close to a deadline, a cash sale lets you pick a closing date that lands before the next one. Tell the buyer which date matters most, whether that is a tax due date, a lease end or a move.

It also helps to know whether the property tax reduction program or the homeowner's exemption applies to you. The application dates are in the table above, and the treasurer's office can tell you what you already have on file.

Idaho Code section 55-2501 and those that follow make a seller of one to four unit residential property fill out a property condition disclosure form. Known defects go on it, and the duty is the same for a listing or a cash sale. The standard form is in Idaho Code 55-2508.

Cash tends to fit an owner who faces a big repair bill, inherited a house from afar, or has a tenant problem. A house in good repair may do better listed. Our purchases are as-is, with an offer once the details are in. Saying no costs nothing, and no price is promised sight unseen.

Steps are few. Tell us the address, the repairs and any tenant or lien details. An offer follows. On acceptance, a title company closes, clears any loan or unpaid tax from your proceeds and hands you the remainder.

Think about timing too. Many owners in this market wait on a tenant's lease, a probate step or a move out of town. Tell us the date that matters and we can plan the closing around it instead of the other way round.

Have three things ready before you call: your latest Bannock County tax bill, permit records and a repair list. If any of your parcel lies in Power County, say so, so the right office is checked.

faqs.q: When are Bannock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 covers the full year or first half, and June 20 covers the second. Weekend deadlines roll to Monday.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Pocatello property assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Bannock County Board of Equalization by the fourth Monday in June. Assessment notices arrive the first Monday of that month.

faqs.q: Is all of Pocatello in Bannock County?
faqs.a: Mostly, though a piece extends into Power County and uses American Falls Joint School District 381. Verify your parcel before collecting tax and school details.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pocatello house if it needs foundation or roof work?
faqs.a: Yes, as-is means neither needs repair before closing. The seller disclosure form is still required, and it should name the problems you know of.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Pocatello?
faqs.a: The survey median for 2020 to 2024 is $271,000. It averages the whole city, and an individual house can sit above or below it.
